The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To help understand the concept of inflation theory in cosmology, imagine a raisin bread dough rising in an oven. Before baking, the dough is small and dense, with raisins (representing galaxies) close together. As the dough bakes and expands rapidly, the distance between the raisins increases dramatically. This expansion isn't the raisins moving through the dough, but the dough itself stretching. Similarly, inflation theory suggests that the early universe expanded incredibly fast, stretching space itself and pushing distant parts of the universe far apart, much like the rapidly rising dough.
